content:
Apple delivered a stellar performance in September, and the momentum is expected to continue with several long-awaited products slated to debut in October.

#1: MacBook Pro / Ultra touchscreen refresh

The Mac has long kept its distance from touchscreens, but that stance may finally change with the arrival of an all-new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) expected in October.

Apple's next-generation MacBook Pro will feature an all-new industrial design — the first major aesthetic overhaul in five years. Beyond touch support, it is also expected to come with an OLED display, the Dynamic Island, and possibly an optional C2 cellular modem.

The MacBook Pro has not had a new look for quite some time, and the Mac's history of avoiding touchscreens runs even deeper — touch input has long been the industry norm, yet Apple has consistently chosen to skip it. I'm very much looking forward to seeing how touch functionality will enhance the Mac user experience going forward.

#2: Next-generation Apple TV 4K

Apple TV hardware has never gone this long without an update. The current latest model remains the third-generation Apple TV 4K released in 2022, with no successor in sight since then.

Rumours suggest we may finally see a new Apple TV 4K in October, with its biggest selling points being a powerful A19 or A19 Pro processor, as well as support for Siri AI features.

Apple raised prices on most of its products this summer, and the Apple TV was among them. This four-year-old Apple TV 4K now sells for US$199, well above its original US$129 launch price. Hopefully the new model won't come with another price hike.

#3: The "HomePad"

Rumours about a HomePod with a screen have been circulating almost as long as the HomePod itself. After Mark Gurman published a detailed report in 2024, such rumours intensified, and the product has often been referred to as the "HomePad".

The HomePad is a smart display with built-in speakers, reportedly tasked with leading Apple's re-entry into the smart home market. It will run a new operating system that blends elements of iOS, tvOS and watchOS, and will feature a StandBy-like mode.

Siri AI will be at the core of the product, complemented by a built-in camera, customisable widgets, and Apple's own apps including Photos, Notes, Music and Calendar.

Of all the new Apple products launching in October or later, which one are you most looking forward to? Feel free to share in the comments.
